device.name: Hamilton STARlet digital twin (star_sim.RobotEnv, PyLabRobot ChatterBox)

facts.text: star-sim is a simulated Hamilton STARlet built on PyLabRobot; the same protocol runs against a simulated robot (ChatterBox backend) or the physical Hamilton STAR
make_liquid_handler switches PyLabRobot tip tracking and volume tracking on before the deck is built
use_hardware=False selects LiquidHandlerChatterboxBackend(num_channels=num_channels); True selects the STAR backend
The deck is a STARLetDeck with one Hamilton 1000 uL filtered tip rack named tip_rack on a tip carrier
Two 96-well plates named source_plate and dest_plate sit on a plate carrier
RobotEnv defaults to the simulation (use_hardware False) with 8 channels
RobotEnv.setup builds the liquid handler and deck, a TipManager and a PlateMap, then awaits lh.setup()
Each primitive acquires fresh tips, performs one liquid-handling action and drops the tips before it returns
column_transfer picks up tips, aspirates, dispenses and discards the tips in a finally block
_plate_state maps each non-empty well id to its tracked used volume in microlitres
TipManager.remaining counts the tip columns from the cursor on that still hold every tip
The column_transfer agent tool takes a volume of 1 to 1000 uL per channel
The mix_column agent tool takes a volume of 1 to 1000 uL
propose_prime seeds the plate volume trackers with the declared volumes
The project was tested with pylabrobot 0.2.1 and requires pylabrobot>=0.2.1

determinism.notes: the fake's tip and volume bookkeeping is deterministic, but the upstream twin exposes no seed or state snapshot, so no replay claim is made

gaps: bookkeeping only: the fake models PyLabRobot's tip and volume tracking, not motion, timing, liquid classes, offsets, aspiration physics or a browser visualizer
the fake's source plate starts with placeholder liquid in every well; the upstream deck starts empty and its agent seeds volumes with propose_prime, which this package does not expose
well and tip capacities in the fake are placeholders, not the PyLabRobot resource definitions
the fake was not compared with the upstream twin; PyLabRobot was not installed where the gate ran
the upstream composite tools (column_transfer, multi_dispense, serial_transfer, propose_prime), the PlateMap compound records and RobotEnv.reset are not exposed

no failure cleanup: the upstream primitives discard the tips in a finally block (star_sim/primitives.py:65-66); this package leaves them mounted after a failure or an e-stop, so the next operation fails channel_free until the endpoint is restarted

own tip selection: tips are taken from PyLabRobot tip tracking (the first adjacent rows in one column), never through TipManager.next_column, so the TipManager cursor behind tips_remaining_columns is not advanced (the count still drops, because it checks every tip of each column)
multi-channel layout: one call uses one column with strictly increasing rows and no repeated well, as a gantry head requires; the fake models no geometry, channel spacing or X motion
no physical device is modelled; the physical STAR path of the upstream is never reached

measures.description: Tip columns that still hold every tip (TipManager)
measures.name: tips_remaining_columns

safe_state.description: simulated only, no physical device: after an e-stop the runtime latch refuses new operations and no further PyLabRobot step of a running operation is sent, but the step in progress is not interrupted, so an e-stop during an operation is reported SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED; tips and liquid stay where the last completed step left them
